content: Mebendazole is an anti-parasitic medication that works by killing worms. It is prescribed to treat infections caused by roundworms, hookworms, pinworms, whipworms, and other parasitic worms. In some cases, it may be used for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Mebendazole is available as a chewable tablet. It is typically taken twice daily, once in the morning and once in the evening, for three days, or as a single one-time dose. You can chew the tablets, swallow them whole, or crush and mix them with food. In some cases, treatment may need to be repeated after 2 to 3 weeks. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take mebendazole exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Before taking mebendazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to mebendazole or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially carbamazepine (Tegretol), phenytoin (Dilantin), and any vitamins. Let your doctor know if you have or have ever had stomach or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking mebendazole, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Mebendazole may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience severe or persistent symptoms such as diarrhea or stomach pain. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to mebendazole. Do not share this medication with anyone else. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If you continue to experience symptoms of infection after completing the course of mebendazole, contact your doctor.
